questions.topic: Section 32: collection of tax on non-taxable supplies
questions.q: A registered dealer adds an amount described as GST to an invoice for a supply on which no tax is payable under the CGST Act. Which rule in section 32(2) applies?
o: No person may collect an amount by way of tax on a supply on which tax is not payable under the Act
A dealer may collect GST if the amount is shown separately
Only the recipient may decide whether GST is collected
The amount may be collected until the annual return is filed
questions.exam: MPSC Inspector of Taxes / DSC East Khasi Hills LDA-cum-Typist / MPSC Secretariat LDA
questions.e: Section 32(2) prohibits any person from collecting an amount by way of tax in respect of a supply of goods or services on which no tax is payable under the Act. Printing “GST” on an invoice does not make a non-taxable supply taxable. Keep this restriction distinct from the rule that a registered person must collect tax only in accordance with the Act and Rules under section 32(1).
questions.source: Original practice; not an official PYQ. India Code, CGST Act, 2017, section 32.
questions.verificationStatus: Checked against the consolidated India Code CGST Act text published 11 June 2026 on 2026-11-17; original practice, not an official PYQ.
questions.label: Original Practice

questions.topic: Section 59: self-assessment
questions.q: A regular registered supplier determines the tax payable for a tax period and furnishes the prescribed return. Which statutory principle under section 59 describes this ordinary process?
o: Assessment by a special audit team
Assessment only by the Appellate Authority
Automatic assessment by the GST Network
questions.exam: MPSC Inspector of Taxes / DSC East Khasi Hills LDA-cum-Typist / MPSC Secretariat LDA
questions.e: Section 59 provides that every registered person shall self-assess the taxes payable under the Act and furnish a return for each tax period as specified in section 39. The taxpayer therefore calculates and declares the liability in the prescribed return; this is different from best-judgment assessment or an audit conducted by the department.
questions.source: Original practice; not an official PYQ. India Code, CGST Act, 2017, section 59.
questions.verificationStatus: Checked against the consolidated India Code CGST Act text published 11 June 2026 on 2026-11-17; original practice, not an official PYQ.

questions.topic: Section 68: inspection of goods in movement
questions.q: A consignment of goods is being transported and the prescribed value threshold is crossed. Under section 68(1) of the CGST Act, who may be required to carry the prescribed documents and devices?
o: The person in charge of the conveyance
questions.exam: MPSC Inspector of Taxes / DSC East Khasi Hills LDA-cum-Typist / MPSC Secretariat LDA
questions.e: Section 68(1) empowers the Government to require the person in charge of a conveyance carrying a consignment above the prescribed value to carry the prescribed documents and devices. The detailed document and e-way-bill requirements are supplied by the Rules. The question tests the statutory responsibility holder, not the person who owns the goods.
questions.source: Original practice; not an official PYQ. India Code, CGST Act, 2017, section 68.

questions.topic: Section 76: amount collected as tax
questions.q: A dealer collects an amount from a customer as GST but later argues that the underlying supply was exempt. What is the general rule under section 76(1) for the amount collected as tax?
o: It may be retained because the supply was exempt
It must be paid to the Government even if the underlying supply is not taxable
It must automatically be refunded by the customer
It becomes the dealer's income after the tax period ends
questions.exam: MPSC Inspector of Taxes / DSC East Khasi Hills LDA-cum-Typist / MPSC Secretariat LDA
questions.e: Section 76(1) requires a person who has collected an amount as representing tax to pay that amount to the Government, irrespective of whether the supplies in respect of which it was collected are taxable. The provision prevents a person from retaining money collected from another person under the description of tax merely by arguing that no tax was actually payable.
questions.source: Original practice; not an official PYQ. India Code, CGST Act, 2017, section 76.

questions.topic: Section 155: burden of proof for input tax credit
questions.q: During proceedings, a registered person asserts that a disputed amount qualifies as input tax credit. Under section 155 of the CGST Act, who bears the burden of proving eligibility for that credit?
o: The proper officer in every case
The person who claims the input tax credit
questions.exam: MPSC Inspector of Taxes / DSC East Khasi Hills LDA-cum-Typist / MPSC Secretariat LDA
questions.e: Section 155 places the burden of proving eligibility for input tax credit on the person who claims the credit. A claim should therefore be supported by the relevant records and evidence. This rule does not remove the officer's duty to follow the Act and natural justice; it identifies who must establish the statutory entitlement to ITC.
questions.source: Original practice; not an official PYQ. India Code, CGST Act, 2017, section 155.

questions.topic: Section 169: service of notices
questions.q: A notice issued under the CGST Act is made available to a registered person on the common portal. Which statement best reflects section 169(1)?
o: Portal availability is a recognised mode of service under the Act
A notice is valid only if delivered personally by the Commissioner
Portal service is valid only after the recipient replies
A notice can be served only through registered post
questions.exam: MPSC Inspector of Taxes / DSC East Khasi Hills LDA-cum-Typist / MPSC Secretariat LDA
questions.e: Section 169(1) lists several recognised modes for serving decisions, orders, summons, notices and other communications. One of them is making the communication available on the common portal. The Act also recognises other prescribed methods, so personal delivery or registered post is not the only possible route.

questions.topic: Section 170: rounding off of tax amounts
questions.q: A sum payable under the CGST Act is calculated as ₹12,345.67. Under section 170, what amount results from statutory rounding to the nearest rupee?
questions.exam: MPSC Inspector of Taxes / DSC East Khasi Hills LDA-cum-Typist / MPSC Secretariat LDA
questions.e: Section 170 requires amounts payable or refundable under the Act to be rounded to the nearest rupee. A fraction of 50 paise or more is increased to the next rupee; a smaller fraction is ignored. Since 67 paise is at least 50 paise, ₹12,345.67 becomes ₹12,346.
questions.source: Original practice; not an official PYQ. India Code, CGST Act, 2017, section 170.
questions.verificationStatus: Checked against the consolidated India Code CGST Act text published 11 June 2026 on 2026-11-17; original practice, not an official PYQ.

questions.topic: Article 143: advisory jurisdiction of the Supreme Court
questions.q: The President refers a question of law or fact of public importance to the Supreme Court under Article 143(1). What may the Supreme Court do?
o: Report its opinion to the President after such hearing as it thinks fit
Appoint the Governor of the State
questions.exam: MPSC Inspector of Taxes / DSC East Khasi Hills LDA-cum-Typist / MPSC Secretariat LDA
questions.e: Article 143(1) permits the President to refer a question of law or fact that has arisen or is likely to arise and is of such public importance that it is expedient to obtain the Supreme Court's opinion. The Court may, after such hearing as it thinks fit, report its opinion to the President. This is advisory jurisdiction, distinct from ordinary contentious litigation.
questions.source: Original practice; not an official PYQ. Legislative Department, Constitution of India, Article 143.
questions.verificationStatus: Checked against the Legislative Department Constitution edition dated 10 September 2026 on 2026-11-17; original practice, not an official PYQ.

questions.topic: Article 131: original jurisdiction of the Supreme Court
questions.q: A legal dispute arises between the Government of India and one or more States concerning a legal right. Which jurisdiction of the Supreme Court is ordinarily relevant under Article 131?
o: Writ jurisdiction of a District Court
questions.exam: MPSC Inspector of Taxes / DSC East Khasi Hills LDA-cum-Typist / MPSC Secretariat LDA
questions.e: Article 131 gives the Supreme Court original jurisdiction, to the exclusion of other courts, in specified disputes between the Government of India and one or more States, or between States, where the existence or extent of a legal right is involved. The Article contains constitutional limits and exclusions; it is not a general appeal provision.
questions.source: Original practice; not an official PYQ. Legislative Department, Constitution of India, Article 131.

questions.topic: Article 243-I: State Finance Commission
questions.q: In a State to which Part IX applies, how often must the Governor constitute a State Finance Commission under Article 243-I to review the financial position of Panchayats?
questions.exam: MPSC Inspector of Taxes / DSC East Khasi Hills LDA-cum-Typist / MPSC Secretariat LDA
questions.e: Article 243-I requires the Governor to constitute a Finance Commission within one year from the commencement of the Constitution (Seventy-third Amendment) Act, 1992, and thereafter at the expiration of every fifth year. The Commission reviews the financial position of Panchayats and makes recommendations on the matters specified in the Article.
questions.source: Original practice; not an official PYQ. Legislative Department, Constitution of India, Article 243-I.

questions.topic: Article 243-J: audit of Panchayat accounts
questions.q: Which constitutional provision authorises the State Legislature to make provisions concerning the maintenance and audit of Panchayat accounts?
questions.exam: MPSC Inspector of Taxes / DSC East Khasi Hills LDA-cum-Typist / MPSC Secretariat LDA
questions.e: Article 243-J provides that, subject to provisions made by the State Legislature, the Legislature may make provisions with respect to the maintenance of accounts by Panchayats and the auditing of those accounts. Do not confuse it with Article 243-I, which concerns the State Finance Commission, or Article 243-K, which concerns Panchayat elections.

questions.topic: Article 243-O: bar to interference in Panchayat elections
questions.q: Which Article bars ordinary court interference in Panchayat electoral matters and provides that a Panchayat election may be challenged only by an election petition in the manner provided by State law?
questions.exam: MPSC Inspector of Taxes / DSC East Khasi Hills LDA-cum-Typist / MPSC Secretariat LDA
questions.e: Article 243-O restricts court interference in matters relating to Panchayat elections. It also provides that an election to a Panchayat may be called in question only by an election petition presented to the authority and in the manner provided by a law made by the State Legislature. The Article deals with election disputes, not reservation, election supervision or the applicability of Part IX.

questions.topic: Partnership: capital multiplied by time
questions.q: A invests ₹40,000 in a business for 6 months, while B invests ₹30,000 for 8 months. If the total profit is ₹24,000, how much should A receive?
questions.exam: MPSC Inspector of Taxes / DSC East Khasi Hills LDA-cum-Typist / MPSC Secretariat LDA
questions.e: In partnership, profit is divided in the ratio of capital multiplied by time. A's contribution is 40,000 × 6 = 2,40,000 and B's is 30,000 × 8 = 2,40,000, so the ratio is 1:1. A therefore receives half of ₹24,000, which is ₹12,000. Always account for the duration as well as the amount invested.
questions.source: Original quantitative aptitude practice; not an official PYQ. NCERT Mathematics textbook portal; calculation independently checked.
questions.verificationStatus: Worked solution, units and reverse check completed on 2026-11-17; original practice, not an official PYQ.

questions.topic: Boats and streams: speed of the current
questions.q: A boat covers 18 km downstream in 2 hours and 12 km upstream in 2 hours. What is the speed of the stream?
questions.exam: MPSC Inspector of Taxes / DSC East Khasi Hills LDA-cum-Typist / MPSC Secretariat LDA
questions.e: Downstream speed = 18 ÷ 2 = 9 km/h; upstream speed = 12 ÷ 2 = 6 km/h. The stream speed is half the difference between these speeds: (9 − 6) ÷ 2 = 1.5 km/h. The still-water boat speed would be their average, 7.5 km/h, which is not what the question asks.
questions.source: Original quantitative aptitude practice; not an official PYQ. NCERT Mathematics textbook portal; calculation independently checked.

questions.topic: Algebraic identities: reciprocal expressions
questions.q: If x − 1/x = 3, where x is non-zero, what is the value of x² + 1/x²?
questions.exam: MPSC Inspector of Taxes / DSC East Khasi Hills LDA-cum-Typist / MPSC Secretariat LDA
questions.e: Square both sides: (x − 1/x)² = 9. Expanding gives x² − 2 + 1/x² = 9. Therefore x² + 1/x² = 9 + 2 = 11. The common error is to forget the middle term −2 when expanding the square of a difference.
questions.source: Original quantitative aptitude practice; not an official PYQ. NCERT Mathematics textbook portal; calculation independently checked.

questions.topic: Probability: drawing without replacement
questions.q: A bag contains 4 red balls and 3 blue balls. Two balls are drawn one after another without replacement. What is the probability that both are red?
questions.exam: MPSC Inspector of Taxes / DSC East Khasi Hills LDA-cum-Typist / MPSC Secretariat LDA
questions.e: There are 7 balls initially. The probability that the first is red is 4/7. After one red ball is removed, 3 red balls remain among 6, so the probability that the second is red is 3/6. Multiply: (4/7) × (3/6) = 12/42 = 2/7. “Without replacement” changes the second denominator and numerator.

questions.topic: Combinations: selecting a committee
questions.q: A committee of 3 members is to be selected from 8 eligible employees. If order does not matter, how many different committees can be formed?
questions.exam: MPSC Inspector of Taxes / DSC East Khasi Hills LDA-cum-Typist / MPSC Secretariat LDA
questions.e: Because the order of selection does not matter, use combinations: ⁸C₃ = 8! ÷ (3! × 5!) = (8 × 7 × 6) ÷ (3 × 2 × 1) = 56. Multiplication by 3! would count the same committee in six different orders, so permutations are not appropriate.

questions.topic: Mensuration: area of a trapezium
questions.q: A trapezium has parallel sides of 14 cm and 22 cm and a perpendicular height of 9 cm. What is its area?
questions.exam: MPSC Inspector of Taxes / DSC East Khasi Hills LDA-cum-Typist / MPSC Secretariat LDA
questions.e: Area of a trapezium = ½ × (sum of the parallel sides) × perpendicular height. Substitute: ½ × (14 + 22) × 9 = ½ × 36 × 9 = 18 × 9 = 162 cm². Use the perpendicular height, not the slant length of a non-parallel side.
questions.source: Original quantitative aptitude practice; not an official PYQ. NCERT Mathematics textbook portal; calculation independently checked.

questions.topic: Clock reasoning: angle between the hands
questions.q: At 4:30, what is the smaller angle between the hour hand and minute hand of a correctly running analogue clock?
questions.exam: MPSC Inspector of Taxes / DSC East Khasi Hills LDA-cum-Typist / MPSC Secretariat LDA
questions.e: At 4:30, the minute hand is at 180° from 12. The hour hand has moved halfway between 4 and 5, so its position is (4 × 30°) + (30 × 0.5°) = 135°. The smaller angle is 180° − 135° = 45°. Remember that the hour hand moves continuously, not in jumps between hour numbers.

questions.topic: Ranking: total number from opposite ranks
questions.q: In a merit list, Rina is ranked 17th from the top and 24th from the bottom. How many candidates are on the list?
questions.exam: MPSC Inspector of Taxes / DSC East Khasi Hills LDA-cum-Typist / MPSC Secretariat LDA
questions.e: When the same person is counted from opposite ends, total candidates = rank from top + rank from bottom − 1. Thus 17 + 24 − 1 = 40. Subtract one because Rina is included in both counts; without the subtraction she would be counted twice.

questions.topic: Calendar: day after a leap year
questions.q: If 1 January 2024 was a Monday, what day of the week was 1 January 2025?
questions.exam: MPSC Inspector of Taxes / DSC East Khasi Hills LDA-cum-Typist / MPSC Secretariat LDA
questions.e: The year 2024 was a leap year and therefore contained 366 days. Since 366 leaves a remainder of 2 when divided by 7, the same calendar date in the next year moves forward by two weekdays. Monday + 2 days = Wednesday.

questions.topic: Excel: filtering records without deleting them
questions.q: An office clerk applies a filter to show only records marked “Pending” in an Excel table. What happens to rows that do not meet the filter condition?
o: They are hidden from the filtered view but remain in the data
They are moved to a new workbook automatically
Their cell values are replaced with blanks
questions.exam: MPSC Inspector of Taxes / DSC East Khasi Hills LDA-cum-Typist / MPSC Secretariat LDA
questions.e: Filtering displays only the rows that meet the selected criteria; rows that do not match are hidden from the current view, not deleted. Clearing the filter makes the hidden rows visible again. Sorting is different: it rearranges the order of records rather than hiding records that fail a condition.

questions.topic: Parallel structure in a series of verbs
questions.q: Choose the word that completes the sentence with correct parallel structure: “The officer was instructed to verify the vouchers, reconcile the ledger, and ___ the report.”
questions.exam: MPSC Inspector of Taxes / DSC East Khasi Hills LDA-cum-Typist / MPSC Secretariat LDA
questions.e: The three coordinated actions share the infinitive marker “to”: to verify, (to) reconcile and (to) file. The final verb should therefore remain in the base form, “file”. “Filing” changes the grammatical form, while “filed” is past tense and breaks the parallel construction.

questions.topic: Dangling modifiers: identifying the doer
questions.q: Choose the sentence that correctly attaches the opening phrase “After checking the entries” to the person who performed the action.
o: After checking the entries, the discrepancy was found by the clerk.
After checking the entries, the clerk found a discrepancy.
The discrepancy, after checking the entries, was found.
After the entries checked, the clerk found a discrepancy.
questions.exam: MPSC Inspector of Taxes / DSC East Khasi Hills LDA-cum-Typist / MPSC Secretariat LDA
questions.e: The opening phrase describes the person who checked the entries. In option B, “the clerk” immediately follows the introductory phrase and is the person who performed the checking. In option A, the grammatical subject is “the discrepancy”, which cannot check entries; that creates a dangling modifier.
questions.source: Original English grammar practice; not an official PYQ. British Council LearnEnglish and Cambridge Dictionary Grammar references.

questions.topic: Gerunds after prepositions
questions.q: Choose the correct form: “The officer apologised for ___ the appointment letter late.”
questions.exam: MPSC Inspector of Taxes / DSC East Khasi Hills LDA-cum-Typist / MPSC Secretariat LDA
questions.e: The word “for” is a preposition, and a preposition is followed by a noun or a gerund when a verb is used. Therefore “sending” is correct. “To send” is an infinitive and does not fit directly after the preposition “for” in this construction.

questions.topic: Punctuation: semicolon with a conjunctive adverb
questions.q: Choose the correctly punctuated sentence.
o: The file was complete, however, the annexure was missing.
The file was complete; however, the annexure was missing.
The file was complete however; the annexure was missing.
The file was complete; however the annexure, was missing.
questions.exam: MPSC Inspector of Taxes / DSC East Khasi Hills LDA-cum-Typist / MPSC Secretariat LDA
questions.e: The sentence contains two independent clauses. A semicolon can separate them, and the conjunctive adverb “however” is followed by a comma: “The file was complete; however, the annexure was missing.” A single comma between the two independent clauses in option A creates a comma splice.

questions.topic: Biology: osmosis in plant root hairs
questions.q: Water enters a plant root-hair cell from the surrounding soil mainly through which process?
questions.exam: MPSC Inspector of Taxes / DSC East Khasi Hills LDA-cum-Typist / MPSC Secretariat LDA
questions.e: Osmosis is the movement of water through a selectively permeable membrane from a region of higher water potential to a region of lower water potential. When the soil solution has a higher water potential than the root-hair cell sap, water enters the cell by osmosis. Mineral-ion uptake may involve active transport, but that is not the process asked here.

questions.topic: Physics: electromagnetic induction
questions.q: A bar magnet is moved towards a coil connected to a sensitive galvanometer, and the galvanometer shows a deflection. Which phenomenon explains the induced current?
questions.exam: MPSC Inspector of Taxes / DSC East Khasi Hills LDA-cum-Typist / MPSC Secretariat LDA
questions.e: Moving the magnet changes the magnetic flux linked with the coil. By Faraday's law, a change in magnetic flux induces an electromotive force; if the circuit is closed, an induced current flows and the galvanometer deflects. A stationary magnet with no change in flux does not produce the same continuing induced effect.

questions.topic: Biology: complementary DNA base pairing
questions.q: In a double-stranded DNA molecule, which nitrogenous base pairs with cytosine?
questions.exam: MPSC Inspector of Taxes / DSC East Khasi Hills LDA-cum-Typist / MPSC Secretariat LDA
questions.e: In DNA, complementary base pairing is specific: adenine pairs with thymine, while cytosine pairs with guanine. A cytosine–guanine pair is held together by three hydrogen bonds. Uracil is normally found in RNA in place of thymine, so it is not the correct DNA partner.

questions.topic: Physical geography: Coriolis effect
questions.q: Because of the Coriolis effect, a freely moving air mass is deflected towards which side of its direction of travel in the Northern Hemisphere?
questions.exam: MPSC Inspector of Taxes / DSC East Khasi Hills LDA-cum-Typist / MPSC Secretariat LDA
questions.e: Earth's rotation produces the Coriolis effect. In the Northern Hemisphere, moving air and other freely moving objects are deflected to the right of their direction of travel; in the Southern Hemisphere, the deflection is to the left. The effect influences large-scale winds and ocean currents, not the initial direction of motion.

questions.topic: Oceanography: spring tides
questions.q: Spring tides generally occur when the Sun, Earth and Moon are aligned during which lunar phases?
questions.exam: MPSC Inspector of Taxes / DSC East Khasi Hills LDA-cum-Typist / MPSC Secretariat LDA
questions.e: Spring tides occur around the new-moon and full-moon phases, when the gravitational effects of the Sun and Moon act along approximately the same line and produce a larger tidal range. The term “spring” refers to the stronger tidal range, not to the season of spring. Neap tides occur near the quarter phases.

questions.topic: Ecological succession: pioneer species on bare rock
questions.q: During primary succession on newly exposed bare rock, which organisms commonly act as pioneer species by helping to initiate soil formation?
questions.exam: MPSC Inspector of Taxes / DSC East Khasi Hills LDA-cum-Typist / MPSC Secretariat LDA
questions.e: Lichens are common pioneer organisms on bare rock. They can colonise exposed surfaces, contribute to weathering and add organic matter as they grow and decompose. Over time, these processes help create conditions in which mosses, herbs, shrubs and eventually larger plant communities may establish. This is primary succession because soil is initially absent.

questions.topic: Ecology: biomagnification of persistent pollutants
questions.q: In a food chain, the concentration of a persistent pollutant such as DDT becomes progressively higher in organisms at successive trophic levels. What is this process called?
questions.exam: MPSC Inspector of Taxes / DSC East Khasi Hills LDA-cum-Typist / MPSC Secretariat LDA
questions.e: Biomagnification is the increase in concentration of a persistent substance in organisms at higher trophic levels of a food chain. A pollutant that is not readily broken down or excreted can accumulate in organisms and become more concentrated in predators that consume many contaminated prey. It is different from bioaccumulation within one organism.

questions.topic: Basic economics: opportunity cost
questions.q: A department uses an unused room as a records store instead of renting it to a training provider. In economic terms, what is the opportunity cost of using the room as a store?
o: The value of the next-best alternative forgone, such as the rent that could have been earned
The total historical cost of constructing the building
The amount of GST charged on office stationery
The accounting depreciation of every asset in the building
questions.exam: MPSC Inspector of Taxes / DSC East Khasi Hills LDA-cum-Typist / MPSC Secretariat LDA
questions.e: Opportunity cost is the value of the next-best alternative that is given up when a choice is made. If renting the room was the best alternative use, the rent that could have been earned is the relevant opportunity cost. It is not necessarily a cash payment and should not be confused with historical cost or depreciation.

questions.topic: Colonial India: Vernacular Press Act
questions.q: The Vernacular Press Act of 1878, directed at publications in Indian languages, was enacted during the viceroyalty of whom?
questions.exam: MPSC Inspector of Taxes / DSC East Khasi Hills LDA-cum-Typist / MPSC Secretariat LDA
questions.e: The Vernacular Press Act was passed in 1878 during Lord Lytton's viceroyalty. It imposed controls on the vernacular press, while English-language publications were exempt. The measure became known as the “Gagging Act” and was later repealed under Lord Ripon. Remember the sequence: Lytton—Act of 1878; Ripon—repeal.

questions.topic: Colonial India: Ilbert Bill controversy
questions.q: What was the central legal issue addressed by the Ilbert Bill controversy of 1883 in British India?
o: Whether Indian judges could try European British subjects in criminal cases
Whether the East India Company could issue its own currency
Whether Indian newspapers could publish in English
Whether provincial legislatures could levy income tax
questions.exam: MPSC Inspector of Taxes / DSC East Khasi Hills LDA-cum-Typist / MPSC Secretariat LDA
questions.e: The Ilbert Bill sought to remove a racial restriction that prevented qualified Indian magistrates and judges from exercising criminal jurisdiction over European British subjects in specified circumstances. The proposal triggered strong opposition from much of the European community and a major controversy over racial equality before the law. The final measure was passed in a compromised form in 1884.
